newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIAN AIRLINES TO FLY TO ST.PETERSBURG.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIAN AIRLINES TO FLY TO ST.PETERSBURG.

text.p: State-run Lithuanian Airlines said on Thursday it will start regular flights to St.Petersburg Russia in May.
"We plan to start three weekly Vilnius - St.Petersburg flights probably, from May 15," the company's director of commerce, Jonas Jutkelis, told Reuters.
"We also want to launch two additional weekly flights to St. Peterburg from the sea resort Palanga in June when vactaion season starts but it will depend on the weather," Jutkelis added.
Jutkelis said that the company's SAAB 340 B will be used to serve the route.
He said that the company had no plans to open other new regular routes this year.
Lithuanian Airlines has 15 regular destinations now to Amsterdam, Berlin, Copenhagen, Dubai, Frankfurt, Istanbul, Helsinki, Kiev, London, Larnaka, Moscow, Paris, Rome, Stockholm and Warsaw.
The company flies three Boeings, eleven Jak-42s and one SAAB 340 B aircraft.
